Text  A. ArcGIS README file for the interactive map of epidemiological, entomological and landscape data for the Kakoi-Koda onchocerciasis focus

The map (available at  https://arcg.is/1PDyO0 ) integrates epidemiological, entomological and landscape data used to analyse  Onchocerca volvulus  transmission dynamics in the Kakoi-Koda onchocerciasis focus,  Ituri  Province, Democratic Republic of  the Congo . Layers are organised by survey year and data type to support exploration of spatial and temporal patterns and to enhance transparency of the analyses presented in the main article.
The map displays:
Anti-Ov16 serological surveys (children, adolescents and adults)
Skin-snip microscopy results (primarily adolescents and adults)
REMO nodule prevalence surveys
Blackfly human landing catches
Blackfly larval and pupal breeding-site inspections, including freshwater crab prospections for  Simulium  neavei

Contextual layers include rivers and basins relevant to onchocerciasis transmission, Mount  Aboro  and surrounding topography, health-zone and health-area boundaries (GRID3 COD), historical land-use/land-cover (Landsat, 1980), and annual forest and dense-forest loss from the Global Forest Change dataset (2001–2024).

Data sources and processing:  All datasets shown in the map were extracted from the epidemiological, entomological and programme sources listed in Table 1 of the main article, including published studies and  data  generated within the NSETHIO research programme  reported here for the first time (available on S1 Dataset) . Data were harmonised into a single master dataset with standardised variables, geographic identifiers and metadata prior to visualisation, published together with the main article.

Privacy and access:  All data are aggregated at the village level and contain no personal identifiers. The map is publicly accessible and should not require specialised GIS software or institutional login credentials.
Intended use:  The interactive map supports data exploration, interpretation of spatial concordance across data streams, and reproducibility of the findings presented in the accompanying publication.

Text  B. Anti-Ov16 ELISA and concurrent skin-snip microscopy shared by ESPEN (context surrounding the Kakoi-Koda focus)

The serological survey (anti-Ov16 ELISA) shared by ESPEN (Expanded Special Project for Elimination of Neglected Tropical Diseases) was conducted in 2015 in one village per health zone (HZ) across four HZs. The seroprevalence (95% confidence interval, CI) was: 1)  Angumu  HZ,  Udongo  Abira Health Area (HA): 5.2% (11/210; 95% CI: 2.8–8.4%) consistent with the nearby REMO classification of Abira  Areju  HA as non-endemic; 2)  Mahagi  HZ, Tilal HA: 0.3% (1/311; 95% CI: 0.0–2.1%), aligning with the REMO of Tilal as non-endemic; 3)  Nyarambe  HZ,  Ang’Aba  HA: 0.3% (1/302; 95% CI: 0.0–2.1%), confirmed to be beyond the Kakoi-Koda onchocerciasis focus limits according to REMO non-endemic results in  Ang’Aba  and  Nyarambe  Mission HAs;  Rethy  HZ, Libi HA: 27.1% (32/118; 95% CI: 19.5–36.2%) within the broader  Ituri  Sid CDTI programme, outside the Kakoi-Koda focus, and compatible with  REMO hypoendemic classification in nearby Bale HA  [1, 11, 12] .

Across all sites, skin-snip microscopy was negative for  Onchocerca volvulus  (0/941). These findings support non-endemic status in the surveyed localities of  Angumu ,  Mahagi  and  Nyarambe  HZs. In Libi HA ( Rethy  HZ), serology indicates historical exposure of about a quarter of the tested population to  O. volvulus , and the non-detectable patent infection at the time of survey (negative skin snips) likely reflects the impact of ongoing CDTI in that HZ.

The serological survey (anti-Ov16 ELISA) shared by ESPEN (Expanded Special Project for Elimination of Neglected Tropical Diseases) was conducted in 2015 in one village per health zone (HZ) across four HZs. The seroprevalence (95% confidence interval, CI) was: 1)  Angumu  HZ,  Udongo  Abira Health Area (HA): 5.2% (11/210; 95% CI: 2.8–8.4%) consistent with the nearby REMO classification of Abira  Areju  HA as non-endemic; 2)  Mahagi  HZ, Tilal HA: 0.3% (1/311; 95% CI: 0.0–2.1%), aligning with the REMO of Tilal as non-endemic; 3)  Nyarambe  HZ,  Ang’Aba  HA: 0.3% (1/302; 95% CI: 0.0–2.1%), confirmed to be beyond the Kakoi-Koda onchocerciasis focus limits according to REMO non-endemic results in  Ang’Aba  and  Nyarambe  Mission HAs;  Rethy  HZ, Libi HA: 27.1% (32/118; 95% CI: 19.5–36.2%) within the broader  Ituri  Sid CDTI programme, outside the Kakoi-Koda focus, and compatible with  REMO hypoendemic classification in nearby Bale HA  [1, 11, 12] .

Across all sites, skin-snip microscopy was negative for  Onchocerca volvulus  (0/941). These findings support non-endemic status in the surveyed localities of  Angumu ,  Mahagi  and  Nyarambe  HZs. In Libi HA ( Rethy  HZ), serology indicates historical exposure of about a quarter of the tested population to  O. volvulus , and the non-detectable patent infection at the time of survey (negative skin snips) likely reflects the impact of ongoing CDTI in that HZ.

Text  A. ArcGIS README file for the interactive map of epidemiological, entomological and landscape data for the Kakoi-Koda onchocerciasis focus

The map (available at  https://arcg.is/1PDyO0 ) integrates epidemiological, entomological and landscape data used to analyse  Onchocerca volvulus  transmission dynamics in the Kakoi-Koda onchocerciasis focus,  Ituri  Province, Democratic Republic of  the Congo . Layers are organised by survey year and data type to support exploration of spatial and temporal patterns and to enhance transparency of the analyses presented in the main article.
The map displays:
Anti-Ov16 serological surveys (children, adolescents and adults)
Skin-snip microscopy results (primarily adolescents and adults)
REMO nodule prevalence surveys
Blackfly human landing catches
Blackfly larval and pupal breeding-site inspections, including freshwater crab prospections for  Simulium  neavei

Contextual layers include rivers and basins relevant to onchocerciasis transmission, Mount  Aboro  and surrounding topography, health-zone and health-area boundaries (GRID3 COD), historical land-use/land-cover (Landsat, 1980), and annual forest and dense-forest loss from the Global Forest Change dataset (2001–2024).

Data sources and processing:  All datasets shown in the map were extracted from the epidemiological, entomological and programme sources listed in Table 1 of the main article, including published studies and  data  generated within the NSETHIO research programme  reported here for the first time (available on S1 Dataset) . Data were harmonised into a single master dataset with standardised variables, geographic identifiers and metadata prior to visualisation, published together with the main article.

Privacy and access:  All data are aggregated at the village level and contain no personal identifiers. The map is publicly accessible and should not require specialised GIS software or institutional login credentials.
Intended use:  The interactive map supports data exploration, interpretation of spatial concordance across data streams, and reproducibility of the findings presented in the accompanying publication.

Text  B. Anti-Ov16 ELISA and concurrent skin-snip microscopy shared by ESPEN (context surrounding the Kakoi-Koda focus)

The serological survey (anti-Ov16 ELISA) shared by ESPEN (Expanded Special Project for Elimination of Neglected Tropical Diseases) was conducted in 2015 in one village per health zone (HZ) across four HZs. The seroprevalence (95% confidence interval, CI) was: 1)  Angumu  HZ,  Udongo  Abira Health Area (HA): 5.2% (11/210; 95% CI: 2.8–8.4%) consistent with the nearby REMO classification of Abira  Areju  HA as non-endemic; 2)  Mahagi  HZ, Tilal HA: 0.3% (1/311; 95% CI: 0.0–2.1%), aligning with the REMO of Tilal as non-endemic; 3)  Nyarambe  HZ,  Ang’Aba  HA: 0.3% (1/302; 95% CI: 0.0–2.1%), confirmed to be beyond the Kakoi-Koda onchocerciasis focus limits according to REMO non-endemic results in  Ang’Aba  and  Nyarambe  Mission HAs;  Rethy  HZ, Libi HA: 27.1% (32/118; 95% CI: 19.5–36.2%) within the broader  Ituri  Sid CDTI programme, outside the Kakoi-Koda focus, and compatible with  REMO hypoendemic classification in nearby Bale HA  [1, 11, 12] .

Across all sites, skin-snip microscopy was negative for  Onchocerca volvulus  (0/941). These findings support non-endemic status in the surveyed localities of  Angumu ,  Mahagi  and  Nyarambe  HZs. In Libi HA ( Rethy  HZ), serology indicates historical exposure of about a quarter of the tested population to  O. volvulus , and the non-detectable patent infection at the time of survey (negative skin snips) likely reflects the impact of ongoing CDTI in that HZ.

Text  A. ArcGIS README file for the interactive map of epidemiological, entomological and landscape data for the Kakoi-Koda onchocerciasis focus

The map (available at  https://arcg.is/1PDyO0 ) integrates epidemiological, entomological and landscape data used to analyse  Onchocerca volvulus  transmission dynamics in the Kakoi-Koda onchocerciasis focus,  Ituri  Province, Democratic Republic of  the Congo . Layers are organised by survey year and data type to support exploration of spatial and temporal patterns and to enhance transparency of the analyses presented in the main article.
The map displays:
Anti-Ov16 serological surveys (children, adolescents and adults)
Skin-snip microscopy results (primarily adolescents and adults)
REMO nodule prevalence surveys
Blackfly human landing catches
Blackfly larval and pupal breeding-site inspections, including freshwater crab prospections for  Simulium  neavei

Contextual layers include rivers and basins relevant to onchocerciasis transmission, Mount  Aboro  and surrounding topography, health-zone and health-area boundaries (GRID3 COD), historical land-use/land-cover (Landsat, 1980), and annual forest and dense-forest loss from the Global Forest Change dataset (2001–2024).

Data sources and processing:  All datasets shown in the map were extracted from the epidemiological, entomological and programme sources listed in Table 1 of the main article, including published studies and  data  generated within the NSETHIO research programme  reported here for the first time (available on S1 Dataset) . Data were harmonised into a single master dataset with standardised variables, geographic identifiers and metadata prior to visualisation, published together with the main article.

Privacy and access:  All data are aggregated at the village level and contain no personal identifiers. The map is publicly accessible and should not require specialised GIS software or institutional login credentials.
Intended use:  The interactive map supports data exploration, interpretation of spatial concordance across data streams, and reproducibility of the findings presented in the accompanying publication.

Text  B. Anti-Ov16 ELISA and concurrent skin-snip microscopy shared by ESPEN (context surrounding the Kakoi-Koda focus)

The serological survey (anti-Ov16 ELISA) shared by ESPEN (Expanded Special Project for Elimination of Neglected Tropical Diseases) was conducted in 2015 in one village per health zone (HZ) across four HZs. The seroprevalence (95% confidence interval, CI) was: 1)  Angumu  HZ,  Udongo  Abira Health Area (HA): 5.2% (11/210; 95% CI: 2.8–8.4%) consistent with the nearby REMO classification of Abira  Areju  HA as non-endemic; 2)  Mahagi  HZ, Tilal HA: 0.3% (1/311; 95% CI: 0.0–2.1%), aligning with the REMO of Tilal as non-endemic; 3)  Nyarambe  HZ,  Ang’Aba  HA: 0.3% (1/302; 95% CI: 0.0–2.1%), confirmed to be beyond the Kakoi-Koda onchocerciasis focus limits according to REMO non-endemic results in  Ang’Aba  and  Nyarambe  Mission HAs;  Rethy  HZ, Libi HA: 27.1% (32/118; 95% CI: 19.5–36.2%) within the broader  Ituri  Sid CDTI programme, outside the Kakoi-Koda focus, and compatible with  REMO hypoendemic classification in nearby Bale HA  [1, 11, 12] .

Across all sites, skin-snip microscopy was negative for  Onchocerca volvulus  (0/941). These findings support non-endemic status in the surveyed localities of  Angumu ,  Mahagi  and  Nyarambe  HZs. In Libi HA ( Rethy  HZ), serology indicates historical exposure of about a quarter of the tested population to  O. volvulus , and the non-detectable patent infection at the time of survey (negative skin snips) likely reflects the impact of ongoing CDTI in that HZ.

Text  A. ArcGIS README file for the interactive map of epidemiological, entomological and landscape data for the Kakoi-Koda onchocerciasis focus

The map (available at  https://arcg.is/1PDyO0 ) integrates epidemiological, entomological and landscape data used to analyse  Onchocerca volvulus  transmission dynamics in the Kakoi-Koda onchocerciasis focus,  Ituri  Province, Democratic Republic of  the Congo . Layers are organised by survey year and data type to support exploration of spatial and temporal patterns and to enhance transparency of the analyses presented in the main article.
The map displays:
Anti-Ov16 serological surveys (children, adolescents and adults)
Skin-snip microscopy results (primarily adolescents and adults)
REMO nodule prevalence surveys
Blackfly human landing catches
Blackfly larval and pupal breeding-site inspections, including freshwater crab prospections for  Simulium  neavei

Contextual layers include rivers and basins relevant to onchocerciasis transmission, Mount  Aboro  and surrounding topography, health-zone and health-area boundaries (GRID3 COD), historical land-use/land-cover (Landsat, 1980), and annual forest and dense-forest loss from the Global Forest Change dataset (2001–2024).

Data sources and processing:  All datasets shown in the map were extracted from the epidemiological, entomological and programme sources listed in Table 1 of the main article, including published studies and  data  generated within the NSETHIO research programme  reported here for the first time (available on S1 Dataset) . Data were harmonised into a single master dataset with standardised variables, geographic identifiers and metadata prior to visualisation, published together with the main article.

Privacy and access:  All data are aggregated at the village level and contain no personal identifiers. The map is publicly accessible and should not require specialised GIS software or institutional login credentials.
Intended use:  The interactive map supports data exploration, interpretation of spatial concordance across data streams, and reproducibility of the findings presented in the accompanying publication.

Text  B. Anti-Ov16 ELISA and concurrent skin-snip microscopy shared by ESPEN (context surrounding the Kakoi-Koda focus)

The serological survey (anti-Ov16 ELISA) shared by ESPEN (Expanded Special Project for Elimination of Neglected Tropical Diseases) was conducted in 2015 in one village per health zone (HZ) across four HZs. The seroprevalence (95% confidence interval, CI) was: 1)  Angumu  HZ,  Udongo  Abira Health Area (HA): 5.2% (11/210; 95% CI: 2.8–8.4%) consistent with the nearby REMO classification of Abira  Areju  HA as non-endemic; 2)  Mahagi  HZ, Tilal HA: 0.3% (1/311; 95% CI: 0.0–2.1%), aligning with the REMO of Tilal as non-endemic; 3)  Nyarambe  HZ,  Ang’Aba  HA: 0.3% (1/302; 95% CI: 0.0–2.1%), confirmed to be beyond the Kakoi-Koda onchocerciasis focus limits according to REMO non-endemic results in  Ang’Aba  and  Nyarambe  Mission HAs;  Rethy  HZ, Libi HA: 27.1% (32/118; 95% CI: 19.5–36.2%) within the broader  Ituri  Sid CDTI programme, outside the Kakoi-Koda focus, and compatible with  REMO hypoendemic classification in nearby Bale HA  [1, 11, 12] .

Across all sites, skin-snip microscopy was negative for  Onchocerca volvulus  (0/941). These findings support non-endemic status in the surveyed localities of  Angumu ,  Mahagi  and  Nyarambe  HZs. In Libi HA ( Rethy  HZ), serology indicates historical exposure of about a quarter of the tested population to  O. volvulus , and the non-detectable patent infection at the time of survey (negative skin snips) likely reflects the impact of ongoing CDTI in that HZ.

Text  A. ArcGIS README file for the interactive map of epidemiological, entomological and landscape data for the Kakoi-Koda onchocerciasis focus

The map (available at  https://arcg.is/1PDyO0 ) integrates epidemiological, entomological and landscape data used to analyse  Onchocerca volvulus  transmission dynamics in the Kakoi-Koda onchocerciasis focus,  Ituri  Province, Democratic Republic of  the Congo . Layers are organised by survey year and data type to support exploration of spatial and temporal patterns and to enhance transparency of the analyses presented in the main article.
The map displays:
Anti-Ov16 serological surveys (children, adolescents and adults)
Skin-snip microscopy results (primarily adolescents and adults)
REMO nodule prevalence surveys
Blackfly human landing catches
Blackfly larval and pupal breeding-site inspections, including freshwater crab prospections for  Simulium  neavei

Contextual layers include rivers and basins relevant to onchocerciasis transmission, Mount  Aboro  and surrounding topography, health-zone and health-area boundaries (GRID3 COD), historical land-use/land-cover (Landsat, 1980), and annual forest and dense-forest loss from the Global Forest Change dataset (2001–2024).

Data sources and processing:  All datasets shown in the map were extracted from the epidemiological, entomological and programme sources listed in Table 1 of the main article, including published studies and  data  generated within the NSETHIO research programme  reported here for the first time (available on S1 Dataset) . Data were harmonised into a single master dataset with standardised variables, geographic identifiers and metadata prior to visualisation, published together with the main article.

Privacy and access:  All data are aggregated at the village level and contain no personal identifiers. The map is publicly accessible and should not require specialised GIS software or institutional login credentials.
Intended use:  The interactive map supports data exploration, interpretation of spatial concordance across data streams, and reproducibility of the findings presented in the accompanying publication.

Text  B. Anti-Ov16 ELISA and concurrent skin-snip microscopy shared by ESPEN (context surrounding the Kakoi-Koda focus)

The serological survey (anti-Ov16 ELISA) shared by ESPEN (Expanded Special Project for Elimination of Neglected Tropical Diseases) was conducted in 2015 in one village per health zone (HZ) across four HZs. The seroprevalence (95% confidence interval, CI) was: 1)  Angumu  HZ,  Udongo  Abira Health Area (HA): 5.2% (11/210; 95% CI: 2.8–8.4%) consistent with the nearby REMO classification of Abira  Areju  HA as non-endemic; 2)  Mahagi  HZ, Tilal HA: 0.3% (1/311; 95% CI: 0.0–2.1%), aligning with the REMO of Tilal as non-endemic; 3)  Nyarambe  HZ,  Ang’Aba  HA: 0.3% (1/302; 95% CI: 0.0–2.1%), confirmed to be beyond the Kakoi-Koda onchocerciasis focus limits according to REMO non-endemic results in  Ang’Aba  and  Nyarambe  Mission HAs;  Rethy  HZ, Libi HA: 27.1% (32/118; 95% CI: 19.5–36.2%) within the broader  Ituri  Sid CDTI programme, outside the Kakoi-Koda focus, and compatible with  REMO hypoendemic classification in nearby Bale HA  [1, 11, 12] .

Across all sites, skin-snip microscopy was negative for  Onchocerca volvulus  (0/941). These findings support non-endemic status in the surveyed localities of  Angumu ,  Mahagi  and  Nyarambe  HZs. In Libi HA ( Rethy  HZ), serology indicates historical exposure of about a quarter of the tested population to  O. volvulus , and the non-detectable patent infection at the time of survey (negative skin snips) likely reflects the impact of ongoing CDTI in that HZ.

Text  A. ArcGIS README file for the interactive map of epidemiological, entomological and landscape data for the Kakoi-Koda onchocerciasis focus

The map (available at  https://arcg.is/1PDyO0 ) integrates epidemiological, entomological and landscape data used to analyse  Onchocerca volvulus  transmission dynamics in the Kakoi-Koda onchocerciasis focus,  Ituri  Province, Democratic Republic of  the Congo . Layers are organised by survey year and data type to support exploration of spatial and temporal patterns and to enhance transparency of the analyses presented in the main article.
The map displays:
Anti-Ov16 serological surveys (children, adolescents and adults)
Skin-snip microscopy results (primarily adolescents and adults)
REMO nodule prevalence surveys
Blackfly human landing catches
Blackfly larval and pupal breeding-site inspections, including freshwater crab prospections for  Simulium  neavei

Contextual layers include rivers and basins relevant to onchocerciasis transmission, Mount  Aboro  and surrounding topography, health-zone and health-area boundaries (GRID3 COD), historical land-use/land-cover (Landsat, 1980), and annual forest and dense-forest loss from the Global Forest Change dataset (2001–2024).

Data sources and processing:  All datasets shown in the map were extracted from the epidemiological, entomological and programme sources listed in Table 1 of the main article, including published studies and  data  generated within the NSETHIO research programme  reported here for the first time (available on S1 Dataset) . Data were harmonised into a single master dataset with standardised variables, geographic identifiers and metadata prior to visualisation, published together with the main article.

Privacy and access:  All data are aggregated at the village level and contain no personal identifiers. The map is publicly accessible and should not require specialised GIS software or institutional login credentials.
Intended use:  The interactive map supports data exploration, interpretation of spatial concordance across data streams, and reproducibility of the findings presented in the accompanying publication.

Text  B. Anti-Ov16 ELISA and concurrent skin-snip microscopy shared by ESPEN (context surrounding the Kakoi-Koda focus)

The serological survey (anti-Ov16 ELISA) shared by ESPEN (Expanded Special Project for Elimination of Neglected Tropical Diseases) was conducted in 2015 in one village per health zone (HZ) across four HZs. The seroprevalence (95% confidence interval, CI) was: 1)  Angumu  HZ,  Udongo  Abira Health Area (HA): 5.2% (11/210; 95% CI: 2.8–8.4%) consistent with the nearby REMO classification of Abira  Areju  HA as non-endemic; 2)  Mahagi  HZ, Tilal HA: 0.3% (1/311; 95% CI: 0.0–2.1%), aligning with the REMO of Tilal as non-endemic; 3)  Nyarambe  HZ,  Ang’Aba  HA: 0.3% (1/302; 95% CI: 0.0–2.1%), confirmed to be beyond the Kakoi-Koda onchocerciasis focus limits according to REMO non-endemic results in  Ang’Aba  and  Nyarambe  Mission HAs;  Rethy  HZ, Libi HA: 27.1% (32/118; 95% CI: 19.5–36.2%) within the broader  Ituri  Sid CDTI programme, outside the Kakoi-Koda focus, and compatible with  REMO hypoendemic classification in nearby Bale HA  [1, 11, 12] .

Across all sites, skin-snip microscopy was negative for  Onchocerca volvulus  (0/941). These findings support non-endemic status in the surveyed localities of  Angumu ,  Mahagi  and  Nyarambe  HZs. In Libi HA ( Rethy  HZ), serology indicates historical exposure of about a quarter of the tested population to  O. volvulus , and the non-detectable patent infection at the time of survey (negative skin snips) likely reflects the impact of ongoing CDTI in that HZ.
